claim_to_avoid: The twenty-mile rule bars these licences.
reason: The rule was repealed effective 1 January 2026 by P.A. 25-101 sections 15 to 17. It supports no current compliance finding of any kind.
safer_language: Former CGS 21a-420u(f), repealed effective 1 January 2026, applied between 1 July 2023 and 31 December 2025. As a historical question the record shows [x].

reason: No public Connecticut record establishes legal or beneficial ownership of any cannabis establishment. Across 4,702 typed relationships there is not one ownership edge.
safer_language: Company A is filed as a principal of Company B in the Secretary of the State registry. A principal filing proves the filing, not ownership, a percentage or control.

claim_to_avoid: A contribution or an award caused a decision.
reason: Contributions, awards and event attendance are lawful, disclosed and ordinary. Sequence is not causation and the record does not support a causal claim.
safer_language: X contributed $N on [date]; the decision followed on [date]. No link between the two is established and none is asserted.

claim_to_avoid: The social equity ventures are fronts.
reason: Neither limb of the statutory test can be checked from outside: no ownership percentage is published and control was not defined until 1 November 2026.
safer_language: Whether these ventures meet the fifty per cent ownership and control test cannot be determined from any public Connecticut record, in either direction.

claim_to_avoid: Operator X has N per cent of the Connecticut cannabis market.
reason: Connecticut publishes no sales or revenue by licensee. Any market share figure is unsourceable.
safer_language: Operator X holds N of the M active retail credentials, which is licence concentration, not market share.

claim_to_avoid: The lottery was won by X.
reason: The published applicant list records entries bought, not awards made.
safer_language: X appears in the published lottery applicant list with N entries. The list does not record awards.

claim_to_avoid: A witness’s position is what the committee report says it is.
reason: Joint favorable reports summarize testimony in committee staff’s words.
safer_language: The committee report characterises the testimony as [x]; the witness’s own filing says [y].

claim_to_avoid: The requirement is in the regulations.
reason: Many adult-use requirements sit in an agency policy document, not in regulations adopted under chapter 54.
safer_language: The requirement appears in the Department’s Policies and Procedures, which is not a regulation adopted under chapter 54.

claim_to_avoid: The bill’s sponsor wrote this language.
reason: Bill status records give introducers and LCO numbers, not drafting authorship.
safer_language: The language first appears in [instrument] on [date]. Who requested it is unknown on this record; the earliest source found is [x].

claim_to_avoid: This agency failed to adopt required regulations.
reason: Whether a regulation was required, and by when, depends on the enabling section and any later amendment. State the section and the date before the conclusion.
safer_language: [Section] directed the agency to adopt regulations by [date]. The eRegulations record shows [status] as of [date].
